newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: PNG prime minister Skate announces interim cabinet.
newsitem.headline: PNG prime minister Skate announces interim cabinet.

text.p: Newly-elected Papua New Guinea prime minister Bill Skate named a caretaker cabinet on Wednesday which he said boasted both experience and fresh faces.
But Skate said the ministers might not retain their places in the full cabinet to be announced next Tuesday.
Skate, the governor of Port Moresby district, swept to power on Tuesday at the head an unlikely coalition of parties including some he once labelled corrupt.
Skate said he had not yet settled on a deputy leader.
"We have in the interim cabinet a mix of both experience and new leaders," Skate told reporters.
"This is only temporary and each party in the coalition will be asked to write to me for final allocation of ministries."
Two of the most significant figures in the coalition were rewarded with ministries in the interim cabinet, while former deputy prime minister Chris Haiveta remained prominent.
People's Democratic Movement leader Roy Yaki was rewarded with two of the most senior ministries in finance and mining and petroleum, as well as justice and health.
People's Progressive Party (PPP) leader Andrew Vaing won the agriculture and livestock, public service, housing and correctional services portfolios.
The PPP and the Pangu party were the basis of the former ruling coalition of ousted prime minister Sir Julius Chan.
Haiveta, the former finance minister, was given a raft of portfolios including foreign affairs and commerce and industry.
Skate vowed after his election on Tuesday that he would launch an anti-corruption drive to root out corruption.
Chan's was one of few governments to run its full term since the country won independence from Australia in 1975.

But a failed plan to hire mercenaries to put down an island rebellion dogged its final stages and a voter backlash saw more than 50 parliamentarians and fifteen former ministers -- including Chan -- lose their seats.
Ron May, a senior fellow in the Australian National University's School of Pacific and Asian Studies, said Skate faced a difficult task in holding the new coalition together.
"We have no reason to suspect it's going to be any more stable than governments before it," May said.
Resolving the nine-year crisis on Bougainville island shapes as Skate's biggest task, just as it had been for Chan.
New Zealand recently hosted two weeks of peace talks between rebels and the government-backed Bougainville administration.
The New Zealand government said on Tuesday the rebels would soon release five PNG soldiers held hostage since September, 1996, as a sign of goodwill.
Thousands have died in the Bougainville conflict since landowners revolted in 1988 over damage caused by the huge Panguna copper mine and royalties they received from it.
